# How to Choose a Janitorial Service in Walnut Creek

> A checklist for Walnut Creek offices hiring a cleaning company: write the scope, prepare for the walkthrough, read proposals closely and compare prices fairly.

## How do you choose a janitorial service in Walnut Creek?

Decide what you want cleaned before you call anyone. When every company quotes the same rooms, tasks and visit schedule, the differences between quotes become easy to see. A monthly total on its own tells you little about the work behind it.

[Our Walnut Creek service page](https://rangeljanitorial.com/locations/walnut-creek) covers the East Bay communities we serve, the cleaning services we offer and how to ask for a free quote. Use the steps below to get ready.

## Start with a written scope

Walk your office with a notepad first. Note roughly how large each area is, the hours people are in the building and anything that gets missed today.

- Workstations and private offices: whether desks are cleared at night and which surfaces should be wiped.
- Conference rooms: tables, chairs, glass and any equipment the crew should not touch.
- Restrooms: fixtures, counters, mirrors, partitions and floors, plus who restocks soap and paper.
- Break rooms: counters, sinks, tables, appliance exteriors and floors. Ask whether the inside of the refrigerator or microwave is part of the price.
- Trash and recycling: which bins are emptied and where the bags go.
- Floors: carpet, tile or other surfaces, and whether deeper floor work is a separate project.

Our [office cleaning](https://rangeljanitorial.com/services/office-cleaning) and [janitorial cleaning](https://rangeljanitorial.com/services/janitorial-cleaning) pages describe common tasks. A service name is only a label; the proposal for your space should spell out the work.

## What to point out during the walkthrough

A walkthrough lets the cleaning team see the space before putting a price on it. Keep your scope list in hand so nothing is skipped.

- Rooms the crew should skip, such as locked offices, server closets or storage.
- Surfaces or finishes that need particular care.
- The time you want cleaning done and the days the office is busiest.
- How the crew gets in: keys, badges, alarm instructions and a contact if something fails.
- Anything the team still needs to know before writing the quote.

## Reading a cleaning proposal

A good proposal answers your questions without a follow-up call. Lay the proposals from different companies next to each other and check each of these points.

- Which areas and tasks are included, and what is left out.
- How often the crew comes and at what time.
- Who supplies trash liners, soap and paper products.
- Routine cleaning listed separately from one-time or periodic projects.
- The price, how it is billed and how changes to the scope get approved.
- Who to contact about a question, a missed task or a schedule change.

## Comparing prices fairly

Quotes are only comparable when they cover the same work. If two totals are far apart, ask which part differs: the area cleaned, the number of restrooms, the floor surfaces, supplies or the time of day. A price per square foot you saw elsewhere is not a quote for your office.

To get a rough number before anyone visits, try our [cleaning calculator](https://rangeljanitorial.com/quote/walnut-creek#cleaning-calculator). Your actual quote is set after the walkthrough.

## Questions to ask before service starts

Find out how you report a missed task, ask for extra cleaning or move the schedule, and who answers when you do. Settling this early makes small problems quick to fix.
